newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU candidates must meet Maastricht criteria-Finland.
newsitem.headline: EMU candidates must meet Maastricht criteria-Finland.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Monday he hoped as many countries as possible would join EMU in 1999 but they must first meet the Maastricht treaty criteria to ensure the stability of the single currency, the euro.
Lipponen was speaking to reporters during a visit to Brussels where he met European Union Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy and other senior EU officials.
Lipponen said his government was determined to prepare the country for membership in the first wave of nations taking part in economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.
Economic data published by the European Commission last week showed that Finland would meet all Maastricht treaty criteria in 1997, the key year for qualifying for EMU in 1999.
De Silguy had stated that Finland "in all respects" was likely to be among the first countries in EMU, Lipponen said.

Parliament will have the final say on whether Finland wants to join, and its vote is expected in early 1998 before a scheduled meeting of EU heads of state and government, which is due to make the final decision on which countries will join EMU from day one.
Lipponen said Finnish preparations were on schedule.
"The government is determined that Finland could be among the first to enter EMU," Lipponen said. "We are doing everything to prepare things."
Asked how many countries he believed would be in EMU from the start, Lipponen said:

"We hope of course that there will be as many countries as possible...but it is also necessary for the sake of stability of the common currency, the euro, for the sake of stability of the international monetary system, that every country should meet the criteria."
He declined to comment on the prospects for individual countries of joining EMU.
Lipponen was due to meet European Commission President Jacques Santer later on Monday.
